questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I was going to go on exchange no matter what, I thought I might as well go all in and go to a place I always wanted to have time to explore.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult, but there was a lot of people I could ask for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was students helping us fill out some of the paperwork and there was an assembly giving out all the information we needed. There was also offices and I was assigned a tutor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm room with shared kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was shared kitchens, but there was not a lot of kitchen equipment, which made cooking difficult if you wanted to do more than reheating food in a microwave and didn't want to invest in buying a lot of kitchen equipment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The bedding provided by the dorm is convenient, as it includes duvet, pillow, and covers for it, but either bring a pillow or buy one, because the ones provided are sandbags.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit hard to make social interactions in the kitchen, because we weren't allowed to eat in there or go to other kitchens than our own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to email every individual professor we wanted to take classes from and get their permission. Then we had to register the courses to a website, print out a paper, get the signature from one of the instructors in charge of exchange students and the professor we were assigned. Then we had to hand over that paper to a particular office.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find the email addresses for all the professors, even though there was email support where we could ask for help with that.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to register for all but two of the classes I originally wanted to take, but found two other classes instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you're a graduate student, make sure to register all your graduate courses with a [G] on the website, or you will have to redo it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very different depending on the individual professor. All courses had at least one presentation, but for some classes they took a lot of preparation and you had to present for an hour and a half.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot more classes to be a full time student, and there was not a lot of lectures. There was less of a reason to take notes during class than what I'm used to, and less of a focus on exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative culture, Critical theory, Early modern Japanese literature, Media Discourse II, New Perspectives on Modern Japanese Literature, Space and Gender in Popular culture, Japanese culture and society in tourism context, Identity making in global consumer culture.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Media Discourse II was a lot of fun and the professor was really nice. We had a lot of freedom to research a topic we found interesting. New perspectives on modern Japanese Literature was also very insightful and interesting, even if the expectations for the students were also a big high.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The extra cost of withdrawing money from ATMs. I would suggest that anyone starts with at least 300,000 yen in cash that they withdrew from their private bank to avoid some the expenses involved with money withdrawal.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were clubs and sports, but I didn't go to any of those, because I was too busy studying. There was also parties and social events to get to know local students, and the school festival.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to the social events because you get to make friends there, which is hard otherwise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of places to see in Nagoya and the nearby cities. I would also suggest a one day trip to Kobe, especially if you want a Danish hotdog. There's a place for that in Suma, Kobe.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There was some challenges, but I made it through.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, go to the social events and install Line on your phone.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The study culture was very different and hard to get accustomed to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are generally friendly and polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Decide if you're going to take a Japanese class or not, even if you won't get any credits or ECTS points for it. When you go to the Ward Office to register your address and sign up for health insurance, either go with a group or someone who knows Japanese. Make a large cash withdrawal in yen from your bank of at least 300,000 yen.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you look nice in the picture you submit to the host institution as it will be used for a lot of things.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Whenever I managed to have a conversation in Japanese.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping and midterms.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
